simple.meaning: כְּתַל (kᵉthal) is a Hebrew object word meaning “wall.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 5:8. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כְּתַל (H3797) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: כְּתַל (kᵉthal) / H3797 is traced through Ezra 5:8, Daniel 5:5 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Be it known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is built with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls. This work goes on with diligence and prospers in their hands.

timeline.evidenceText: Be it known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is built with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls. This work goes on with diligence and prospers in their hands.
In the same hour, the fingers of a man’s hand came out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace. The king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
